newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Four units of S.Korea Kia go limit-down on report.
newsitem.headline: Four units of S.Korea Kia go limit-down on report.

text.p: Shares of four units of South Korea's Kia Group went limit-down in the afternoon on a report the government may allow a state-run bank to take over Kia Motors, brokers said on Tuesday.
A finance ministry spokesman denied the report.
Kia Motors lost 1,200 won to 14,000, Asia Motors fell 430 won to 5,020, Kisan shed 440 to 5,170 and Kia Service fell 440 to 5,060.

The Munhwa Ilbo said the government planned to exclude Kia Motors from an unofficial bank bailout programme and instead push it into court receivership, if the nation's eighth-largest conglomerate did not meet creditor demands.
"Investors believe court receivership means bankruptcy and the takeover process by the state bank would take forever," said a broker at LG Securities.
The daily said the government would let Korea Development Bank take over Kia Motors as its subsidiary.

Most of Kia's six listed affiliates' shares had already been hit in early trading on news that emergency loans from creditors would only be given if presidents of Kia affiliates tendered resignations and the labour union agreed in writing to a wage freeze and workforce reduction.
